# Private Pilot Certificate for AEA Technicians

## Sponsored by Sporty’s Foundation and AEA Educational Foundation <u>SCHOLARSHIP APPLICATION Award: $6,000</u>

#### Completed applications must be received by April 1, 2027 – no exceptions

## AWARD INFORMATION / ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS

1. Applicant must be employed by an AEA Regular Member for no less than one year as an avionics technician or avionics manager.
2. Award money is to be used for achieving **PRIVATE PILOT CERTIFICATE.** The award money is not intended for use in achieving any other rating or certificate.
3. Award money is to be used for flight training costs only.
4. Award recipient must plan to begin pilot training within six months of receiving scholarship.
5. Award money will be sent to repair station manager for disbursement.
6. Email application, essay and employer recommendation: **[contact redacted]**
## APPLICATION PROCEDURE

1. Write an essay of not more than 200 words explaining, “Why you believe having a pilot’s license will benefit your employer.” <u>Important: essay must be typed and double spaced.</u>
2. Submit the attached letter of recommendation as completed by your employer.

### Employer Recommendation Form for Sporty’s Private Pilot Certificate Scholarship


This scholarship will be used to pursue a private pilot's certificate. Please provide your views of the applicant

### as a person, as well as an employee.

### Poor Good Excellent

### average or excellent.

### an additional sheet if necessary.

evidence.excerpt:
## Scholarships for Prospective Students

The Davidson Honors College (DHC) offers merit-based scholarships to incoming students to recognize outstanding talent, academic performance, and leadership potential. These are the University of Montana's premier academic scholarships and include the Presidential Leadership Scholarship (PLS), Provost’s Honors Scholarship (PHS), and the Dean’s Leadership Scholarship (DLS).

These scholarships reduce the cost of attendance at the University of Montana and students who meet progression standards may have their awards renewed for up to four years.

We are looking for well-rounded, ambitious, and curious learners. While we look at academic performance and achievements, these criteria are not absolute and all highly motivated students are encouraged to apply.

Montana high school graduates should also apply for the [Montana University System Honors Scholarship](https://mus.edu/Prepare/Pay/Scholarships/MUS_Honor_Scholarship.html).

- [Step 1: Apply to UM](https://umontana.edu/how-to-apply/process/undergraduate.php)
- [Step 2: Apply to DHC](https://beagriz.umontana.edu/portal/bear_tracks)

## Scholarship Details

- The Fine Print

Scholarships may be waivers or donor funds. Some of the largest donor awards may defray the cost of attendance beyond tuition. All scholarship funds will be awarded based on donor criteria and available awards.

  - Maximum PLS Scholarships waivers are offered using the following criteria:
    - [Non-resident student tuition](https://www.umt.edu/finaid/cost-of-attendance/bachelors-deg-COA/out-of-state-coa.php) may be waived to the [WUE tuition rate](https://www.umt.edu/finaid/cost-of-attendance/bachelors-deg-COA/wue-coa.php).
    - WUE tuition may be waived to the [in-state tuition rate](https://www.umt.edu/finaid/cost-of-attendance/bachelors-deg-COA/in-state-coa.php).
    - Montana residents may have tuition fully waived by [certain eligible waiversPDF (PDF document)](https://mus.edu/borpol/bor900/940-13.pdf).


      - All Montana residents wishing to be considered for DHC scholarships must apply for the [Montana University System Honor Scholarship](https://www.mus.edu/Prepare/Pay/Scholarships/MUS_Honor_Scholarship.html). Students will retain the PLS, PHS, or DLS title if they use the MUS Honor Scholarship.
  - No waivers or combination of waivers may exceed the cost of tuition.
  - Waivers decrease across the scholarship tiers (PHS and DLS).
  - No applications received after December 1 at 11:59 PM MST will be considered for incoming student scholarships.

- Renewal Criteria

Students who are requesting renewal of the PLS, PHS, or DLS will be reviewed using the following criteria:

  - Making adequate progress in the honors college, which is defined as taking at least two honors experiences per academic year, including the completion of Introduction to Honors in your first year.

  - Maintaining at least a 3.4 cumulative GPA. If GPA is below 3.4, students may appeal to provide additional context and outline a plan to elevate their GPA. If students continue to fall short of the expectations of scholars, their scholarship may be withdrawn.

  - Completing an average of 30 credits per academic year/be on track for completion within four years.

  - Attending at least one 1:1 or group advising or career development session per academic year.

  - Demonstrate the highest standards of academic and personal integrity.

  - Be in good standing with the University of Montana.


## Important Dates

- DHC Scholarship Deadline and Review Process

  - Be in good standing with the University of Montana.

evidence.excerpt:
## Scholarships for Prospective Students

The Davidson Honors College (DHC) offers merit-based scholarships to incoming students to recognize outstanding talent, academic performance, and leadership potential. These are the University of Montana's premier academic scholarships and include the Presidential Leadership Scholarship (PLS), Provost’s Honors Scholarship (PHS), and the Dean’s Leadership Scholarship (DLS).

These scholarships reduce the cost of attendance at the University of Montana and students who meet progression standards may have their awards renewed for up to four years.

We are looking for well-rounded, ambitious, and curious learners. While we look at academic performance and achievements, these criteria are not absolute and all highly motivated students are encouraged to apply.

Montana high school graduates should also apply for the [Montana University System Honors Scholarship](https://mus.edu/Prepare/Pay/Scholarships/MUS_Honor_Scholarship.html).

- [Step 1: Apply to UM](https://umontana.edu/how-to-apply/process/undergraduate.php)
- [Step 2: Apply to DHC](https://beagriz.umontana.edu/portal/bear_tracks)

## Scholarship Details

- The Fine Print

Scholarships may be waivers or donor funds. Some of the largest donor awards may defray the cost of attendance beyond tuition. All scholarship funds will be awarded based on donor criteria and available awards.

  - Maximum PLS Scholarships waivers are offered using the following criteria:
    - [Non-resident student tuition](https://www.umt.edu/finaid/cost-of-attendance/bachelors-deg-COA/out-of-state-coa.php) may be waived to the [WUE tuition rate](https://www.umt.edu/finaid/cost-of-attendance/bachelors-deg-COA/wue-coa.php).
    - WUE tuition may be waived to the [in-state tuition rate](https://www.umt.edu/finaid/cost-of-attendance/bachelors-deg-COA/in-state-coa.php).
    - Montana residents may have tuition fully waived by [certain eligible waiversPDF (PDF document)](https://mus.edu/borpol/bor900/940-13.pdf).


      - All Montana residents wishing to be considered for DHC scholarships must apply for the [Montana University System Honor Scholarship](https://www.mus.edu/Prepare/Pay/Scholarships/MUS_Honor_Scholarship.html). Students will retain the PLS, PHS, or DLS title if they use the MUS Honor Scholarship.
  - No waivers or combination of waivers may exceed the cost of tuition.
  - Waivers decrease across the scholarship tiers (PHS and DLS).
  - No applications received after December 1 at 11:59 PM MST will be considered for incoming student scholarships.

- Renewal Criteria

Students who are requesting renewal of the PLS, PHS, or DLS will be reviewed using the following criteria:

  - Making adequate progress in the honors college, which is defined as taking at least two honors experiences per academic year, including the completion of Introduction to Honors in your first year.

  - Maintaining at least a 3.4 cumulative GPA. If GPA is below 3.4, students may appeal to provide additional context and outline a plan to elevate their GPA. If students continue to fall short of the expectations of scholars, their scholarship may be withdrawn.

  - Completing an average of 30 credits per academic year/be on track for completion within four years.

  - Attending at least one 1:1 or group advising or career development session per academic year.

  - Demonstrate the highest standards of academic and personal integrity.

  - Be in good standing with the University of Montana.


## Important Dates

- DHC Scholarship Deadline and Review Process

To apply to the Davidson Honors College, you must first apply to and be accepted by the University of Montana. To ensure adequate time for admission to UM and time to complete your DHC application by the scholarship deadline, it is recommended you apply to the University of Montana by November 24. The DHC application due date for scholarship consideration is December 1. DHC Applications received by 11:59 PM (MST) on December 1 will be considered for the Incoming Student Scholarships: Presidential Leadership Scholarship (PLS), Provost Honors Scholarship (PHS), and Dean’s Leadership Scholarship (DLS).

Applications received after that date will be considered for admission to the Davidson Honors College, but NOT for the Incoming Student Scholarships. Davidson Honors College applications will be considered only from those who have applied for admission to a four-year undergraduate program at the University of Montana.

Applications received before December 1 will be reviewed by a scholarship committee between December and January. Students will be notified if they have been invited to interview in mid-late January. Interviews will be conducted virtually in mid-February. Students will be notified of scholarship offers by mid-March and have until May 1 to notify us of their plans to accept or decline the offer.

evidence.excerpt:
## Using Scholarships to Help Fund Your Education

A scholarship is money awarded to help pay for your education that does not have to repaid. Scholarships can come from UM and its academic departments, private organizations, nonprofits, employers and other sources. Criteria for each scholarship will vary and may be based on things like academic achievement, talent, financial need, leadership or specific interests.

### Scholarship Application Timelines

New students are automatically evaluated for the merit-based scholarships when they apply. In order to be considered for incoming merit scholarships, students must apply for admission by **July 1**. Scholarship priority will be given to those who apply by this date.

It is best to begin researching scholarship opportunities in the fall for the following academic year as the majority of scholarship applications have a winter deadline.

## Find Scholarships at UM

- [Scholarship Universe](https://www.umt.edu/student-financial-services/scholarships/apply-for-scholarships.php)

The University of Montana uses Scholarship Universe to help students find, apply for and accept scholarship opportunities across campus.

- [Scholarships for New Students](https://www.umt.edu/student-financial-services/scholarships/scholarships-new-students/default.php)

Incoming students are eligible for several scholarships at UM, including the UM Academic Achievement Scholarship, the Western Undergraduate Exchange tuition discount and others.

- [Scholarships for Current Students](https://www.umt.edu/student-financial-services/scholarships/scholarships-current-students/default.php)

Current students at UM are eligible for many scholarship opportunities. Learn more about scholarships for currently enrolled students.

- [External Scholarships](https://www.umt.edu/student-financial-services/scholarships/external-scholarships.php)

External organizations awarded hundreds of thousands in scholarship dollars to UM students each year. Learn more about finding and applying for external scholarships.

- [MUS Scholarships](https://awardmontana.mus.edu/index.html#scholarships)

The Montana University System offers various scholarships to students meeting certain criteria. Visit the MUS website to learn more about their scholarship opportunities.

- [Scholarship Appeals](https://www.umt.edu/student-financial-services/scholarships/scholarship-appeals.php)

Extenuating circumstances that can warrant the review of an award decision. Learn how current students and admitted students can appeal a scholarship decision.

The Davidson Honors College (DHC) offers merit-based scholarships to incoming students to recognize outstanding talent, academic performance, and leadership potential. These are the University of Montana's premier academic scholarships and include the Presidential Leadership Scholarship (PLS), Provost’s Honors Scholarship (PHS), and the Dean’s Leadership Scholarship (DLS).

These scholarships reduce the cost of attendance at the University of Montana and students who meet progression standards may have their awards renewed for up to four years.

- [Step 1: Apply to UM](https://umontana.edu/how-to-apply/process/undergraduate.php)
- [Step 2: Apply to DHC](https://beagriz.umontana.edu/portal/bear_tracks)

## Scholarship Details

- The Fine Print

Scholarships may be waivers or donor funds. Some of the largest donor awards may defray the cost of attendance beyond tuition. All scholarship funds will be awarded based on donor criteria and available awards.

  - Maximum PLS Scholarships waivers are offered using the following criteria:
    - [Non-resident student tuition](https://www.umt.edu/finaid/cost-of-attendance/bachelors-deg-COA/out-of-state-coa.php) may be waived to the [WUE tuition rate](https://www.umt.edu/finaid/cost-of-attendance/bachelors-deg-COA/wue-coa.php).
    - WUE tuition may be waived to the [in-state tuition rate](https://www.umt.edu/finaid/cost-of-attendance/bachelors-deg-COA/in-state-coa.php).
    - Montana residents may have tuition fully waived by [certain eligible waiversPDF (PDF document)](https://mus.edu/borpol/bor900/940-13.pdf).


      - All Montana residents wishing to be considered for DHC scholarships must apply for the [Montana University System Honor Scholarship](https://www.mus.edu/Prepare/Pay/Scholarships/MUS_Honor_Scholarship.html). Students will retain the PLS, PHS, or DLS title if they use the MUS Honor Scholarship.
  - No waivers or combination of waivers may exceed the cost of tuition.
  - Waivers decrease across the scholarship tiers (PHS and DLS).
  - No applications received after December 1 at 11:59 PM MST will be considered for incoming student scholarships.

- Renewal Criteria

Students who are requesting renewal of the PLS, PHS, or DLS will be reviewed using the following criteria:

  - Making adequate progress in the honors college, which is defined as taking at least two honors experiences per academic year, including the completion of Introduction to Honors in your first year.

  - Maintaining at least a 3.4 cumulative GPA. If GPA is below 3.4, students may appeal to provide additional context and outline a plan to elevate their GPA. If students continue to fall short of the expectations of scholars, their scholarship may be withdrawn.

  - Completing an average of 30 credits per academic year/be on track for completion within four years.

  - Attending at least one 1:1 or group advising or career development session per academic year.

  - Demonstrate the highest standards of academic and personal integrity.

  - Be in good standing with the University of Montana.

evidence.excerpt:
## Using Scholarships to Help Fund Your Education

A scholarship is money awarded to help pay for your education that does not have to repaid. Scholarships can come from UM and its academic departments, private organizations, nonprofits, employers and other sources. Criteria for each scholarship will vary and may be based on things like academic achievement, talent, financial need, leadership or specific interests.

### Scholarship Application Timelines

New students are automatically evaluated for the merit-based scholarships when they apply. In order to be considered for incoming merit scholarships, students must apply for admission by **July 1**. Scholarship priority will be given to those who apply by this date.

It is best to begin researching scholarship opportunities in the fall for the following academic year as the majority of scholarship applications have a winter deadline.

## Find Scholarships at UM

- [Scholarship Universe](https://www.umt.edu/student-financial-services/scholarships/apply-for-scholarships.php)

The University of Montana uses Scholarship Universe to help students find, apply for and accept scholarship opportunities across campus.

- [Scholarships for New Students](https://www.umt.edu/student-financial-services/scholarships/scholarships-new-students/default.php)

Incoming students are eligible for several scholarships at UM, including the UM Academic Achievement Scholarship, the Western Undergraduate Exchange tuition discount and others.

- [Scholarships for Current Students](https://www.umt.edu/student-financial-services/scholarships/scholarships-current-students/default.php)

Current students at UM are eligible for many scholarship opportunities. Learn more about scholarships for currently enrolled students.

- [External Scholarships](https://www.umt.edu/student-financial-services/scholarships/external-scholarships.php)

External organizations awarded hundreds of thousands in scholarship dollars to UM students each year. Learn more about finding and applying for external scholarships.

- [MUS Scholarships](https://awardmontana.mus.edu/index.html#scholarships)

The Montana University System offers various scholarships to students meeting certain criteria. Visit the MUS website to learn more about their scholarship opportunities.

- [Scholarship Appeals](https://www.umt.edu/student-financial-services/scholarships/scholarship-appeals.php)

Extenuating circumstances that can warrant the review of an award decision. Learn how current students and admitted students can appeal a scholarship decision.

      - All Montana residents wishing to be considered for DHC scholarships must apply for the [Montana University System Honor Scholarship](https://www.mus.edu/Prepare/Pay/Scholarships/MUS_Honor_Scholarship.html). Students will retain the PLS, PHS, or DLS title if they use the MUS Honor Scholarship.
  - No waivers or combination of waivers may exceed the cost of tuition.
  - Waivers decrease across the scholarship tiers (PHS and DLS).
  - No applications received after December 1 at 11:59 PM MST will be considered for incoming student scholarships.

- Renewal Criteria

Students who are requesting renewal of the PLS, PHS, or DLS will be reviewed using the following criteria:

  - Making adequate progress in the honors college, which is defined as taking at least two honors experiences per academic year, including the completion of Introduction to Honors in your first year.

  - Maintaining at least a 3.4 cumulative GPA. If GPA is below 3.4, students may appeal to provide additional context and outline a plan to elevate their GPA. If students continue to fall short of the expectations of scholars, their scholarship may be withdrawn.

  - Completing an average of 30 credits per academic year/be on track for completion within four years.

  - Attending at least one 1:1 or group advising or career development session per academic year.

  - Demonstrate the highest standards of academic and personal integrity.

  - Be in good standing with the University of Montana.


## Important Dates

- DHC Scholarship Deadline and Review Process

To apply to the Davidson Honors College, you must first apply to and be accepted by the University of Montana. To ensure adequate time for admission to UM and time to complete your DHC application by the scholarship deadline, it is recommended you apply to the University of Montana by November 24. The DHC application due date for scholarship consideration is December 1. DHC Applications received by 11:59 PM (MST) on December 1 will be considered for the Incoming Student Scholarships: Presidential Leadership Scholarship (PLS), Provost Honors Scholarship (PHS), and Dean’s Leadership Scholarship (DLS).

Applications received after that date will be considered for admission to the Davidson Honors College, but NOT for the Incoming Student Scholarships. Davidson Honors College applications will be considered only from those who have applied for admission to a four-year undergraduate program at the University of Montana.

Applications received before December 1 will be reviewed by a scholarship committee between December and January. Students will be notified if they have been invited to interview in mid-late January. Interviews will be conducted virtually in mid-February. Students will be notified of scholarship offers by mid-March and have until May 1 to notify us of their plans to accept or decline the offer.

A scholarship is money awarded to help pay for your education that does not have to repaid. Scholarships can come from UM and its academic departments, private organizations, nonprofits, employers and other sources. Criteria for each scholarship will vary and may be based on things like academic achievement, talent, financial need, leadership or specific interests.

New students are automatically evaluated for the merit-based scholarships when they apply. In order to be considered for incoming merit scholarships, students must apply for admission by **July 1**. Scholarship priority will be given to those who apply by this date.

It is best to begin researching scholarship opportunities in the fall for the following academic year as the majority of scholarship applications have a winter deadline.

Extenuating circumstances that can warrant the review of an award decision. Learn how current students and admitted students can appeal a scholarship decision.

# Equitable Excellence Scholarship® Program

Equitable Foundation has established the Equitable Excellence Scholarship® Program to assist public high school seniors who are planning to continue their education at a two-year or four-year college in the United States by Fall 2027.

[image omitted]

Applications Open - Deadline December 22, 2026 3:00 PM CT

Apply [query-bearing locator withheld]

## Equitable Excellence Scholarship®

Equitable is committed to students who show potential: those with the courage to pursue what’s possible; who display strength in managing challenges; who share wisdom with others. The Equitable Excellence Scholarship® is celebrating 24 years of providing funding to students who are dedicated to achieving their dreams.

This program is administered by Scholarship America®, the nation’s largest designer and manager of scholarship and other education support programs for corporations, foundations, associations, and individuals. Eligibility for individual programs is determined at the sole discretion of the sponsor and eligible applications are reviewed by Scholarship America’s evaluation team. In compliance with Federal law, this program will not discriminate in the terms, conditions, or privileges of participation on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, disability, or sexual orientation.

## Eligibility

**Applicants to the Equitable Excellence Scholarship® Program must:**

- Be current high school seniors at a public\* high school in one of the 50 U.S. states, the District of Columbia, or Puerto Rico
- Plan to enroll full-time in an accredited two-year or four-year college or university in the United States for the entire upcoming academic year
- Demonstrate ambition and self-drive to give back to their communities by encouraging other students to pursue post-secondary attainment
- Be willing to provide a release to publicize their identities and information about their plans or achievements, along with photographs, for use in program promotion and information
- Have a minimum 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale

\*Applicants from private or home schools are not eligible to apply.

Employees, associates, financial professionals, or immediate family members of employees, associates, or financial professionals of Equitable, Equitable Advisors and all Equitable affiliated companies or Scholarship America, or their affiliates, subsidiaries, or advertising and promotion agencies, are not eligible to apply to this program.

## Awards

The authorized distribution for new awards is up to $500,000. Up to 100 renewable awards of $5,000 each will be granted.

- $5,000 awards are renewable up to three years or until a bachelor’s degree is earned, whichever occurs first, on the basis of satisfactory academic performance and continued enrollment, and
- A $500 gift card will be awarded to each recipient’s educator of choice to be used for professional development activities or classroom supplies.

Sponsor will require recipients to attend the virtual Equitable Excellence Senior Leader Meet & Greet and at least two (2) professional development workshops each year of college (4 years) during their renewable scholarship timeline.

Students who have previously received the scholarship and wish to renew will receive an email invitation to renew their scholarship in January and should not complete a new application.

Awards are for undergraduate study only.

### **Notification**

All applicants will be notified in early spring.

**IMPORTANT:** Notifications are sent via email. When setting up your account, avoid using a school or work email. Instead, use an active, personal email address that you will continue to have access to.

### **Payment of Scholarships**

Scholarship America processes scholarship payments on behalf of Equitable Foundation. Payment is made in August.

### **Selection of Recipients**

Scholarship recipients are selected on the basis of:

- Financial need – applicants must have financial need
- Academic performance
- Leadership and participation in school and community activities, awards, and honors
- Work experience
- Unusual personal or family circumstances
- A personal statement\* that demonstrates ambition and self-drive to give back to the community by encouraging other students to pursue post-secondary attainment

**\*Personal statement topic**

_“Working towards your college degree can lead to economic mobility and create a positive impact on you and those around you. How will you, as a college graduate, plan to pay it forward and inspire others in your community to work towards their own college degree?”_

Selection of recipients is made by Scholarship America.

In no instance does any officer or employee of Equitable Foundation play a part in the selection. Not all applicants to the program will be selected as recipients.

All applicants agree to accept the decision as final.

## Requirements

**As part of your application, you must upload the following:**

- A current, complete transcript of grades. Grade reports are not accepted. Transcripts must display:
  - Student name
  - School name
  - Grades
  - Credit hours for each course and term in which each course was taken.
- Copy of the first two pages of the most recently filed IRS Form 1040 used for the Financial Information section of the application. Please black out all social security numbers and bank account information.

Your application is **not** complete unless all required materials are submitted electronically.

# Horatio Alger Montana Undergraduate Scholarship Program

This scholarship program is made possible through the generosity of <PRIVATE_PERSON> and <PRIVATE_PERSON> in partnership with the Horatio Alger Association.

[Contact Association](https://scholars.horatioalger.org/about-us/contact-us/)

[image omitted]

## Scholarship Recipients Will Receive Up to $15,000

Over 4 Years Seniors at Montana high schools who want to go to college now have more help in reaching that goal.

The program, administered by the Horatio Alger Association, is specifically for students who have confronted and overcome adversity in their young lives. Students from across Montana will be selected to each receive a $15,000 scholarship and have the honor of being named as a Horatio Alger Montana Scholar.

[recipient caption omitted]

[image omitted]

## Scholarship Affiliates

Scholarships can be utilized to pursue higher education at the University of Montana, Montana State University, or one of their affiliates:

**University of Montana Western**

**Missoula College – University of Montana**

**Helena College – University of Montana**

**Montana Technological University in Butte**

**Montana State University Billings**

**Montana State University Northern**

**Great Falls College – Montana State University**

## Frequently Asked Questions

##### What is the scholarship application submission deadline?

The submission deadline to apply for the Horatio Alger Montana Undergraduate Scholarship Program is **February 15th** for high school seniors and **March 1st** for high school juniors.

##### How do I apply for the scholarship?

Applications are submitted only via the Horatio Alger Association’s application page during the window of **December 1st to February 15th** (for high school seniors) and **December 1st to March 1st** (for high school juniors).

If you have previously submitted an application to Horatio Alger for their National Scholarship, your application will automatically be considered for the Horatio Alger Dennis & Phyllis Washington Undergraduate Scholarship.

##### What are the eligibility requirements?

1. BE ENROLLED FULL TIME AS A HIGH SCHOOL SENIOR IN MONTANA, progressing toward graduation in Spring/Summer 2026, with plans to enter a college in the Montana University System no later than the fall following graduation.
2. BE INVOLVED in co-curricular, after school, or community activities.
3. DEMONSTRATE CRITICAL FINANCIAL NEED. Students of families who are eligible for the Pell Grant are strongly encouraged to apply.
4. DISPLAY INTEGRITY AND PERSEVERANCE in overcoming adversity.
5. BE A UNITED STATES CITIZEN.
6. PURSUE & COMPLETE A BACHELOR’S DEGREE IN THE MONTANA UNIVERSITY SYSTEM. Students may start their studies at a two-year institution and then transfer to a four-year institution. Eligible Institutions Include:

##### What universities participate in this scholarship program?

The University of Montana, or one of its afﬁliates:

- Helena College
- Missoula College
- University of Montana Western (Dillon)
- Montana Technological University (Butte)

Montana State University, or one of its afﬁliates:

- Great Falls College – Montana State University
- Montana State University Billings
- Montana State University Northern (Havre)

##### What are the requirements to maintain the scholarship once awarded?

All recipients must maintain a Grade Point Average (GPA) of 2.0 to keep their scholarship.

evidence.excerpt:
# Horatio Alger Montana Undergraduate Scholarship Program

This scholarship program is made possible through the generosity of <PRIVATE_PERSON> and <PRIVATE_PERSON> in partnership with the Horatio Alger Association.

[Contact Association](https://scholars.horatioalger.org/about-us/contact-us/)

[image omitted]

## Scholarship Recipients Will Receive Up to $15,000

Over 4 Years Seniors at Montana high schools who want to go to college now have more help in reaching that goal.

The program, administered by the Horatio Alger Association, is specifically for students who have confronted and overcome adversity in their young lives. Students from across Montana will be selected to each receive a $15,000 scholarship and have the honor of being named as a Horatio Alger Montana Scholar.

[recipient caption omitted]

[image omitted]

## Scholarship Affiliates

Scholarships can be utilized to pursue higher education at the University of Montana, Montana State University, or one of their affiliates:

**University of Montana Western**

**Missoula College – University of Montana**

**Helena College – University of Montana**

**Montana Technological University in Butte**

**Montana State University Billings**

**Montana State University Northern**

**Great Falls College – Montana State University**

## Frequently Asked Questions

##### What is the scholarship application submission deadline?

The submission deadline to apply for the Horatio Alger Montana Undergraduate Scholarship Program is **February 15th** for high school seniors and **March 1st** for high school juniors.

##### How do I apply for the scholarship?

Applications are submitted only via the Horatio Alger Association’s application page during the window of **December 1st to February 15th** (for high school seniors) and **December 1st to March 1st** (for high school juniors).

If you have previously submitted an application to Horatio Alger for their National Scholarship, your application will automatically be considered for the Horatio Alger Dennis & Phyllis Washington Undergraduate Scholarship.

##### What are the eligibility requirements?

1. BE ENROLLED FULL TIME AS A HIGH SCHOOL SENIOR IN MONTANA, progressing toward graduation in Spring/Summer 2026, with plans to enter a college in the Montana University System no later than the fall following graduation.
2. BE INVOLVED in co-curricular, after school, or community activities.
3. DEMONSTRATE CRITICAL FINANCIAL NEED. Students of families who are eligible for the Pell Grant are strongly encouraged to apply.
4. DISPLAY INTEGRITY AND PERSEVERANCE in overcoming adversity.
5. BE A UNITED STATES CITIZEN.
6. PURSUE & COMPLETE A BACHELOR’S DEGREE IN THE MONTANA UNIVERSITY SYSTEM. Students may start their studies at a two-year institution and then transfer to a four-year institution. Eligible Institutions Include:

##### What universities participate in this scholarship program?

The University of Montana, or one of its afﬁliates:

- Helena College
- Missoula College
- University of Montana Western (Dillon)
- Montana Technological University (Butte)

Montana State University, or one of its afﬁliates:

- Great Falls College – Montana State University
- Montana State University Billings
- Montana State University Northern (Havre)

##### What are the requirements to maintain the scholarship once awarded?

All recipients must maintain a Grade Point Average (GPA) of 2.0 to keep their scholarship.

evidence.excerpt:
Incoming first year and transfer students can access the First Generation Award application on the CSU Scholarship Application in RamWeb. The FGA First Year application opens October 1st and closes February 1st for first year students. The FGA Transfer application opens October 1st and closes June 1st for transfer students.×

## **Purpose of FGA**

The purpose of the program is to encourage participation in higher education by first generation college students who have significant financial need (as defined by standard calculations based on financial aid application information).

CSU defines a “first generation college student” as someone whose parents/guardians have not completed a bachelor’s degree. For students whose parents/guardians completed a degree outside of the United States, please contact us to confirm eligibility. Siblings do not impact how CSU defines first generation.

## **Award Amount**

The First Generation Award Program is an extremely competitive process, with hundreds of applicants each year, and a limited number of awards available. CSU funds 75 awards per year and there can be additional donor funded awards based on the application year.

- The FGA base award amount is $5,000 annually and is renewable for up to 5 years contingent upon full-time enrollment at the Fort Collins campus.
- First Generation Award recipients are eligible for an additional $3,000 Partnership Award through the Community for Excellence (C4E). The Partnership Award is an annual award that is renewable for up to 5 years.
  - Note: Students can earn a Partnership Award through different partners but can only receive one,  non-stackable, Partnership Award.  The FGA base award can still be received even if the student will receive a Partnership Award through a different partner.

## **Eligibility Requirements**

- Be a **first generation student,** someone whose parents/guardians have not completed a bachelor’s degree.
- Be a **newly admitted first-year or transfer student** in a degree program at Colorado State University-Fort Collins campus by April 1st. (We recommend that you apply for admission by the priority application filing date)

1. Note: Current CSU students, full-time CSU Online students, and/or CSU-Global students are not eligible to apply.
2. Plan to enroll full-time at Colorado State University, Fort Collins campus the summer or fall of the application year. Full-time enrollment implies that a student is enrolled in at least 12 regular on-campus credits per semester.
3. The award is not available for new students entering CSU in the spring semester.

- Student has not previously earned a bachelor’s degree.
- Demonstrate potential for **academic success** (as reflected by a high school or transfer Grade Point Average).
- Document **financial need** according to the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at [fafsa.gov](http://www.fafsa.gov/)  OR the Colorado Application for State Financial Aid (CASFA).
- Be a legal resident of Colorado; **OR** classified as an in-state resident for tuition purposes; **OR** be eligible to receive the Native American Legacy Award (https://admissions.colostate.edu/nativeamerican/).

## **Application Requirements**

The First Generation Award application is available through RamWeb. There is a **FGA First Year application** that is open October 1st through February 1st. There is also a **FGA Transfer application** that is open October 1st through June 1st. Students must be admitted to CSU to access RamWeb. Once in RamWeb, search for the CSU Scholarship Application (CSUSA). You must FIRST complete the Colorado State University Scholarship Application (CSUSA) through Academic Works before you can search for the FGA application. Please be sure to prepare enough time to complete BOTH applications. A complete application consists of the CSUSA General App, FGA Application, and FGA essay responses.

Additionally, students must complete a financial aid application to complete the FGA application process. Please note that the deadline to submit the financial aid application is one month before the First Generation Award application deadline.

- Complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at [fafsa.gov](http://www.fafsa.gov/) by February 1st of the year you plan to enroll. List Colorado State University as a school choice to receive the results of your FAFSA. **Our school code is 001350**. Submit any additional documents requested by the Office of Financial Aid as soon as possible.
- Alternatively, if eligible, you can complete the Colorado Application for State Financial Aid (CASFA) by March 1 of the year you plan to enroll. See your [RAMweb.colostate.edu](http://ramweb.colostate.edu/), Financial Aid Requirements page for further information or contact the Office of Financial Aid with questions.

## **What happens after I apply?**

- Incomplete applications will NOT be considered. You may or may not be notified that your application is incomplete until the selection process is over, so we recommend that you check your application carefully to be sure it is complete prior to submitting it to the University. The selection committee will review all completed materials submitted by the application deadline.
- The selection process for First Year applicants begins early February. First Year applicants will be notified by April 1st if they are selected for the award. Students who are not eligible or are not selected will note receive notice.
- The selection process for Transfer applicants begins early June. Transfer applications will be notified by July 1st if they are selected for the award. Students who are not eligible or are not selected will note receive notice.
- The FGA program does utilize a waitlist so some students may be notified later in the spring if a spot opens up. Students who are not selected will receive notification in early summer.

### Lineworker Scholarships

Flathead Electric Cooperative funds scholarships to assist students looking to become electrical lineworkers. Scholarship applicants must meet these requirements:

  - Student must be enrolled in the [Pre-Apprentice Line Program at Highlands College, Montana Technological University](https://mtech.edu/lineprogram/index.html) and fulfill all admission requirements.
  - Student’s hometown must be in the [service territory](https://www.flatheadelectric.com/about-my-co-op/how-were-governed/board-of-trustees/district-map/) of Flathead Electric Co-op. This includes:
    - Kalispell
    - Whitefish
    - Bigfork
    - Columbia Falls
    - Libby
    - Cooke City
  - Upon admission to the Pre-Apprentice Line Program, Montana Tech will invite students from Flathead Electric Co-op’s service area to apply for the scholarship and submit an essay on their background, career goals, and financial need.

## Lineworker

Scholarships

### One-Semester Program

Our one-semester Pre-Apprentice Line certificate program prepares you for groundman and apprentice positions within the line trade. You will learn how to assist with the installation, construction, maintenance, and repair of electrical power line systems. Students will also earn their CDL Class A license as part of the program.

Before beginning the behind-the-wheel training for the Class A Commercial Driver’s License, students must complete the three-part Class A Commercial Driver’s License (CDL-A) written permit exam. After successful completion of the behind-the-wheel training requirements for the Class A Commercial Driver’s License (CDL-A) are met, the student must complete the CDL-A skills exam administered by the Montana Motor Vehicle Division, to become a licensed CDL-A driver, before entering the workforce.

### Collaboration with Employers

The program is an ongoing collaborative effort of many organizations who have come together to oversee the program and ensure future line-workers have the skills needed in industry. The Pre-Apprentice Line program combines classroom teaching with extensive, carefully-planned field training.  Students will work with experienced instructors to learn the tasks and skills essential to the trade.  Safety procedures are discussed and practiced with each task.   To participate in this program, you:

- Must not have a fear of heights!
- Should have good manual dexterity.
- Must like to work outdoors in changing weather conditions.
- Be physically fit.
- Weigh less than 275 pounds (bucket trucks have weight limits).

The first week of training will include intensive pole work.

The program space is limited, and first come, first served. Admission to Highlands College does not guarantee admission to the Pre-Apprenticeship Line Program.

### Admission Requirements

The following criteria must be met before admission will be granted to the Pre-Apprentice Line program. Initial admission to the program is based on a first-come first-served process. The first individuals to apply for a specific semester will have a slot reserved pending submission of the remaining items listed below.

1. **Department of Transportation (DOT)** **Physical**: Applicants must complete and pass the DOT physical. Applicants should contact their personal physician to fulfill this requirement. A copy of the completed DOT examination form must be submitted to the Admissions Office [contact redacted]. Please keep your original card. If your physician is not DOT certified you can search for DOT certified physicians by area: [https://nationalregistry.fmcsa.dot.gov/home](https://nationalregistry.fmcsa.dot.gov/home).
2. **Immunization records**: Proof of two doses of Measles, Mumps, Rubella (MMR). Your high school should have these on file or you can check with the Health Department.
3. **Valid driver’s license**: Please submit a copy of your current valid driver’s license.
4. **Official transcripts:** Official high school transcripts and college transcripts (if applicable).
5. **Age**: Applicants must be at least 18 years of age before the first 2 weeks of the semester of study are complete.

The Pre-Apprentice Line Program is unique in that students complete 30 credits in one semester, and students pay tuition and fees that differ from the rest of Highlands College. 2. **CLP (Commercial Learners Permit):** Please make every attempt to obtain your CLP (written permit) **prior** to the start date of the program. **You must pass this written exam and obtain the CLP before you can start driving.** The link to schedule the exam is [https://dojmt.gov/driving/appointments/](https://dojmt.gov/driving/appointments/).

Please note: you must be 18 years of age at the time you take the CDL written exam.
3. **Drug Testing:** The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA), along with the Department of Transportation (DOT), require that individuals subject to the CDL requirements follow alcohol and drug testing rules. Drug testing will be conducted the first week of class, and will be scheduled by Highlands College.
4. **Equipment:** Students will need to bring their own boots and gloves. See FAQ's for more information.

XI OMICRON CHAPTER SCHOLARSHIP
Beta Sigma Phi is an international women’s organization with local chapters in Whitefish
that were established in 1948. We are a cultural, social, and civic sorority, and through
these endeavors our local chapter is pleased to offer a $1,000 scholarship to a deserving
graduating senior from Whitefish High School.
Submission Deadline: Submit to your guidance counselor by 3:00 PM on Friday, April 17,
2026
Award Amount: $1,000
To be considered for this scholarship award, applicants must meet the following criteria and
submit all of the following materials:
1. Formal Resume including:
o Contact information - Name, parents’ names, address, phone, and e-mail. [Field labels only; no values collected.]
o Leadership roles, community service, activities and work experience
2. Statement of Financial Need
Include a statement explaining your financial need. You may mention FAFSA status or
Pell Grant eligibility if applicable.
3. Brief Essay
Describe your educational and career goals and what motivates you to pursue higher
education?.
4. High School Transcript
Submit your Whitefish High School transcript showing a GPA of 2.0 or higher.
5. Postsecondary Application
Provide confirmation that you have applied to an institution of higher learning or
training program in the state of Montana.
6. Letter of Recommendation
One letter from a teacher or mentor.
7. Eligibility Requirement
Applicants may not be the child of a member of Beta Sigma Phi.
Receiving another scholarship will not disqualify a student from being awarded this
scholarship.
Thank you for your interest in our scholarship!

evidence.excerpt:
2026 BETA SIGMA PHI
XI OMICRON CHAPTER SCHOLARSHIP
Beta Sigma Phi is an international women’s organization with local chapters in Whitefish
that were established in 1948. We are a cultural, social, and civic sorority, and through
these endeavors our local chapter is pleased to offer a $1,000 scholarship to a deserving
graduating senior from Whitefish High School.
Submission Deadline: Submit to your guidance counselor by 3:00 PM on Friday, April 17,
2026
Award Amount: $1,000
To be considered for this scholarship award, applicants must meet the following criteria and
submit all of the following materials:
1. Formal Resume including:
o Contact information - Name, parents’ names, address, phone, and e-mail. [Field labels only; no values collected.]
o Leadership roles, community service, activities and work experience
2. Statement of Financial Need
Include a statement explaining your financial need. You may mention FAFSA status or
Pell Grant eligibility if applicable.
3. Brief Essay
Describe your educational and career goals and what motivates you to pursue higher
education?.
4. High School Transcript
Submit your Whitefish High School transcript showing a GPA of 2.0 or higher.
5. Postsecondary Application
Provide confirmation that you have applied to an institution of higher learning or
training program in the state of Montana.
6. Letter of Recommendation
One letter from a teacher or mentor.
7. Eligibility Requirement
Applicants may not be the child of a member of Beta Sigma Phi.
Receiving another scholarship will not disqualify a student from being awarded this
scholarship.
Thank you for your interest in our scholarship!

**How to Apply:**

NTHS members will apply for scholarships through the NTHS Member Portal. Each scholarship has different requirements and application window dates. If you meet the eligibility criteria for a scholarship, click the “Apply” button to read the instructions and begin your application process.

[image omitted]

[Other child programs omitted.]
### **NTHS HOSA Scholarship**

NTHS and HOSA have joined forces to provide seven $1,000 scholarships to dual members of NTHS and HOSA certain to become leaders in the global health community.

**All application questions should be directed to HOSA.**

**Available: January 1 - April 15 \| Number Awarded: 7 \| Amount: $1,000**

[Apply](https://hosa.org/scholarships)

[[image omitted]](https://nths.org/sponsors-partners/)

### **NTHS SkillsUSA Scholarship**

With a goal of supporting promising futures for skilled professionals, career-ready leaders and responsible community members, NTHS proudly partners with SkillsUSA to provide four $1,000 scholarships to students who hold dual membership with NTHS and SkillsUSA.

**All application questions should be directed to SkillsUSA.**

**Available: January 6 - April 15 \| Number Awarded: 4 \| Amount: $1,000**

[Apply](https://apply.mykaleidoscope.com/program/NTHS2026)

[[image omitted]](https://nths.org/sponsors-partners/)

### **NTHS TSA Scholarship**

NTHS is thrilled to join TSA and provide three $1,000 scholarships to dual members engaged in STEM and ready to explore new educational horizons.

**All application questions should be directed to TSA.**

**Available: September 15 - May 1 \| Number Awarded: 3 \| Amount: $1,000**

[Apply](https://tsaweb.org/programs/awards-and-scholarships)

[[image omitted]](https://nths.org/sponsors-partners/)

evidence.excerpt:
##### National Technical Honor Society

Since 1984, the National Technical Honor Society (NTHS) has been the honor society for Career and Technical Education (CTE), serving high schools, career centers, community and technical colleges, and universities. Recognizing over 76,000 new members and awarding nearly $335,000 in scholarships annually, NTHS exists to celebrate and empower students across all CTE areas. NTHS achieves this through career development, leadership development, service, and recognition opportunities at the chapter level. The Technology Student Association (TSA) and NTHS formed a partnership to provide these benefits to TSA members.

At the 2027 National TSA Conference, NTHS will award three (3) $1000 academic scholarships to eligible applicants who hold dual membership with NTHS and TSA.

A TSA student member must be nominated for NTHS membership by a school’s NTHS chapter advisor (the school the student attends must have a current NTHS chapter). Use the links below for details about the benefits of NTHS membership, a directory of current NTHS chapters, and how to establish an NTHS chapter.

- The benefits of NTHS membership - [What We Do - NTHS](https://nths.org/what-we-do/)

- Find out if your school has an NTHS chapter - [Chapter Directory - NTHS](https://nths.org/chapter-directory/)

- How to establish an NTHS chapter - [Learn How to Establish a Chapter - NTHS](https://nths.org/establish-a-chapter/)

Learn more about the National Technical Honor Society at [NTHS.org](https://nths.org/).

The NTHS scholarship application is accessible via the password-protected [Student Member Site](https://tsamembership.registermychapter.com/members) in the TSA Membership System. Students are eligible to apply for the NTHS scholarship if they are current members of TSA and NTHS. Completed applications (with required attachments) should be summitted by email to [contact locator redacted].

- Gather all necessary information and **[complete the online form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1L3C2pIcuTa9-cf7QRX2PPhRhoBqJ78-BczcJFHTtl8M/viewform).**
- Keep your [checklist](https://naehcy.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/2026-NAEHCY-Scholarship-Information-and-Application.docx.pdf) handy and make sure you include all supplemental materials when you are ready to email them to [contact redacted].
- Submit all materials by Friday, July 31, 2026 (by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time).

If you have any questions, please contact us at [contact locator redacted]. Are you looking for additional scholarship resources? [Let us help](https://naehcy.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/2026-NAEHCY-Scholarship-Guide-.docx-1.pdf).

# The NAEHCY Scholars Program

### 2026 Overview

The NAEHCY Scholars Program will award up to ten $3,000 scholarships to postsecondary
students who have experienced homelessness* and are actively pursuing their
post-secondary education. Selected scholars are chosen from a pool of applicants who
meet all eligibility criteria and submit all required materials by the deadline.

Selected scholars are invited, encouraged, and financially supported to attend NAEHCY’s
annual conference (November) where they participate in enrichment and professional
development activities, share their experiences with NAEHCY stakeholders, and participate
in an awards ceremony. NAEHCY Scholars will be invited to participate in two additional
convenings designed to support their educational journey and provide personal and
professional enrichment as well as mentorship opportunities.

Below you will find all of the important information necessary to apply. Please visit our
website at naehcy.org/scholarships/naehcy-scholars-program to learn more about the
program, read the Frequently Asked Questions, and find additional scholarship resources
for students.

### 2026 Important Dates and Deadlines

● May 1, 2026 - Application Opens

● Friday, July 31, 2026 - Application Deadline (by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time)

● By September 1, 2026 - Notification of Awards

● October 31 - November 3, 2026 - Annual Conference in Nashville, TN

### Eligibility

To be eligible for the scholarship, applicants must meet the following criteria:

● Applicants must be under the age of 23, as of July 31, 2026. .

● Applicants must be actively pursuing postsecondary education/trade school.

● Applicants must be eligible for McKinney-Vento assistance or have
experienced homelessness* (while in school) within the last six years.

● Applicants must submit a letter from their McKinney-Vento liaison, verifying
their eligibility. (Liaison should be from their current school district or the
district from which they graduated.)

---

● Applicants may alternately provide eligibility verification from a school official,
outreach worker, shelter provider, religious leader, or other homeless service
provider, confirming current or former homeless status.

● **Please note,** undocumented students who meet the above criteria ARE
eligible. However, **_previous recipients of a NAEHCY scholarship within the
past three years are NOT eligible._**

**The applicant’s homeless status is defined by the federal McKinney-Vento Homeless Education Act, which defines a person
considered to be homeless as one who “lacks a fixed, regular, and adequate night-time residence.” This includes people living
in shelters, cars, motels/hotels, campgrounds, or places not meant for human habitation. The definition includes children
and youth who are living with friends/relatives temporarily (doubled-up) because they lack permanent housing.*

### Terms/Conditions/Requirements

● Submit the <u>application form</u> and all application materials by July 31, 2026 (by
11:59 p.m. Eastern Time) to <u>[contact redacted]</u>.

● Be sure to include a current, working email, not a high school email.

● You will receive an auto-generated email confirmation if you submit your
application form online. You will receive a confirmation email (by September
1) to let you know that you are being considered for an award.

● Incomplete applications will not be considered for an award.

● If selected for an award, you will be required to provide an official copy of your
school’s transcript as well as proof of postsecondary school or program
enrollment prior to the release of funds.

### How to Apply

Applicants will be evaluated on each component of their submission. If sending
multiple emails, make sure to include the applicant’s full name and date of birth
with each message and attachment to ensure our reviewers can accurately identify
materials. Accepted file formats include PDF, Word, JPG and PNG.

### ● <u>Complete the application form online</u>

(Or, complete the form on pg. 3 and email to <u>[contact redacted]</u>.)

● Gather required documents

● Personal essay (guidelines on pg. 4)

● Unofficial transcript (If there are barriers to obtaining a transcript,
contact us at <u>[contact redacted]</u>.)

● Letter verifying current or former homeless status (guidelines on pg. 4)

● Minimum of one letter of recommendation (guidelines on pg. 4)

● Email all required documents to <u>[contact redacted]</u>

● If you need assistance or accommodation, or need a Spanish application,
please contact us at <u>[contact redacted]</u>

---

# 2026 Scholarship Application: Additional Materials

### Personal Essay

Please complete a personal essay (500-800 words, double spaced) that
addresses one of the following questions.

1. What would be the one thing you would change about the educational
system for students experiencing homelessness, and why?

2. If you were an entrepreneur, what would you develop, and why?

3. As you look back, what would be one piece of advice you would give to
someone starting High School, and why?

4. Looking forward, what is something you plan to change about yourself, or
add to your life, and why?

5. What is your biggest challenge? If you woke up tomorrow and that
obstacle was gone, how would you go about your day?

6. What activities or interests do you have that support your educational
goals (i.e. church, community service, sports, the arts, etc.)?

### Recommenders and References

● A letter from your local homeless education liaison, school official, outreach
worker, shelter provider, religious leader, or other homeless service provider,
confirming current or former homeless status. This individual must include
their contact information and signature on the letter.

● A minimum of one letter of recommendation from a teacher, counselor, or
other adult (not related to applicant) that can speak to your qualifications and
experiences. This individual must include their contact information and
signature on the letter.

---

### Tips for Completing Your NAEHCY Scholarship Application and Essay

### ● Be Honest and Reflective

○ Share your personal story authentically. This scholarship honors
resilience, not perfection.

○ Speak from the heart about how your experiences have shaped your
perspective, values, and goals.

### ● Highlight Your Strengths Through Challenges

○ Show how you have navigated obstacles—resilience, responsibility,
adaptability, or leadership in difficult times.

○ Don’t focus only on hardships; emphasize how you respond to
challenges.

### ● Share Your Educational Journey

○ Explain how homelessness or foster care impacted your education.

○ Highlight key academic achievements, even small ones, and moments of
perseverance.

### ● Connect Your Story to Your Future Goals

○ Talk about your dreams for college and career. How has your past shaped
what you want to pursue?

○ Show how receiving this scholarship will help you reach those goals.

### ● Include Moments of Growth

○ Reflect on what you have learned about yourself, others, or the world.

○ Discuss turning points: who helped you? What did you discover about
your own strength?

### ● Don’t Be Afraid to Show Emotion

○ It is okay to show vulnerability; your feelings are part of your journey.

○ Discussing how you have felt helps the reader connect with your story.

### ● Focus on Your Voice

○ Write in your own words, as if you’re telling your story to someone who
truly wants to understand.

○ You don’t need big words; being authentic in your essay is your most
powerful tool.

---

### ● Stay Organized

○ Use a clear structure: introduction, body, and conclusion.

○ Begin with a powerful opening, include key moments in the body, and
end with a hopeful and forward-looking conclusion.

### ● Follow the Prompt and ALL Application Instructions

○ Answer one of the specific questions in the NAEHCY Scholarship
application instructions.

○ Please adhere to the required word count of 500-800 words.

○ Be certain to verify your eligibility as a student who has experienced
homelessness by including a letter from your high school
McKinney-Vento liaison or eligibility verification from a school official,
outreach worker, shelter provider, religious leader, or other homeless
service provider confirming your current or former homeless status.

### ● Ask for Feedback

○ Have a trusted teacher, counselor, or mentor read your draft.

○ They can help catch grammar issues and ensure your message is clear
and compelling.

### ● Proofread Carefully

○ Double-check your application and essay for spelling, grammar, and
clarity.

○ Read your essay out loud to hear how it sounds.

## Q. How do I apply for a scholarship award?

You must submit all of the following materials by the deadline:

- Completed application (<u>click here to submit online</u>)

# 2026 Scholarship Application: Additional Materials

### Personal Essay

Please complete a personal essay (500-800 words, double spaced) that
addresses one of the following questions.

1. What would be the one thing you would change about the educational
system for students experiencing homelessness, and why?

2. If you were an entrepreneur, what would you develop, and why?

3. As you look back, what would be one piece of advice you would give to
someone starting High School, and why?

4. Looking forward, what is something you plan to change about yourself, or
add to your life, and why?

5. What is your biggest challenge? If you woke up tomorrow and that
obstacle was gone, how would you go about your day?

6. What activities or interests do you have that support your educational
goals (i.e. church, community service, sports, the arts, etc.)?

### Recommenders and References

● A letter from your local homeless education liaison, school official, outreach
worker, shelter provider, religious leader, or other homeless service provider,
confirming current or former homeless status. This individual must include
their contact information and signature on the letter.

● A minimum of one letter of recommendation from a teacher, counselor, or
other adult (not related to applicant) that can speak to your qualifications and
experiences. This individual must include their contact information and
signature on the letter.

---

### Tips for Completing Your NAEHCY Scholarship Application and Essay

### ● Be Honest and Reflective

○ Share your personal story authentically. This scholarship honors
resilience, not perfection.

○ Speak from the heart about how your experiences have shaped your
perspective, values, and goals.

### ● Highlight Your Strengths Through Challenges

○ Show how you have navigated obstacles—resilience, responsibility,
adaptability, or leadership in difficult times.

○ Don’t focus only on hardships; emphasize how you respond to
challenges.

### ● Share Your Educational Journey

○ Explain how homelessness or foster care impacted your education.

○ Highlight key academic achievements, even small ones, and moments of
perseverance.

### ● Connect Your Story to Your Future Goals

○ Talk about your dreams for college and career. How has your past shaped
what you want to pursue?

○ Show how receiving this scholarship will help you reach those goals.

### ● Include Moments of Growth

○ Reflect on what you have learned about yourself, others, or the world.

○ Discuss turning points: who helped you? What did you discover about
your own strength?

### ● Don’t Be Afraid to Show Emotion

○ It is okay to show vulnerability; your feelings are part of your journey.

○ Discussing how you have felt helps the reader connect with your story.

### ● Focus on Your Voice

○ Write in your own words, as if you’re telling your story to someone who
truly wants to understand.

○ You don’t need big words; being authentic in your essay is your most
powerful tool.

---

### ● Stay Organized

○ Use a clear structure: introduction, body, and conclusion.

○ Begin with a powerful opening, include key moments in the body, and
end with a hopeful and forward-looking conclusion.

### ● Follow the Prompt and ALL Application Instructions

○ Answer one of the specific questions in the NAEHCY Scholarship
application instructions.

○ Please adhere to the required word count of 500-800 words.

○ Be certain to verify your eligibility as a student who has experienced
homelessness by including a letter from your high school
McKinney-Vento liaison or eligibility verification from a school official,
outreach worker, shelter provider, religious leader, or other homeless
service provider confirming your current or former homeless status.

### ● Ask for Feedback

○ Have a trusted teacher, counselor, or mentor read your draft.

○ They can help catch grammar issues and ensure your message is clear
and compelling.

### ● Proofread Carefully

○ Double-check your application and essay for spelling, grammar, and
clarity.

○ Read your essay out loud to hear how it sounds.

## Q. How do I apply for a scholarship award?

You must submit all of the following materials by the deadline:

- Completed application (<u>click here to submit online</u>)
- Personal essay
- Unofficial school transcript
- Letter verifying current or former homeless status
- A minimum of one letter of recommendation
## Q. How many scholarships will NAEHCY award this year, and for how much?

The NAEHCY Scholars Program will award at least ten scholarships this year of up to $3,000 each to postsecondary students who have experienced homelessness* and are actively pursuing their post-secondary education. Selected scholars are chosen from a pool of applicants who meet all eligibility criteria and submit all required materials by the deadline.

## Q. When is the deadline for submitting an application this year?

Friday, July 31, 2026 (by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time) is the final submission deadline in order to be considered for a scholarship award.

**Q. When are letters of recommendation and school transcripts due? Can they be sent separately from my application?** We strongly encourage you to <u>submit the application form online</u>, and then email all supporting application materials within one email. This helps the NAEHCY staff with processing your materials. Your email should include these four attachments:
- Personal essay
- Unofficial transcript (If there are barriers to obtaining a transcript, contact us at <u>[contact redacted]</u>)
- Letter verifying current or former homeless status
- Minimum of one letter of recommendation
If you send multiple emails, make sure to include the applicant’s full name and date of birth with each message to ensure our reviewers can accurately identify materials.

## Q. What types of files am I allowed to include as attachments?

Accepted file formats include PDF, Word, JPG and PNG.

**Q. Do my letters of verification and recommendation have to be written by teachers, or can they come from anyone?** One letter verifying your current or former homeless status is required and must be from a local homeless education liaison, school official, outreach worker, shelter provider, religious leader, or other homeless service provider. This individual must include their contact information and signature on the letter. Your letter of recommendation may be written by anyone who knows you well and can attest to your experiences, character, leadership ability, commitment to education while homeless, and/or academic achievement. This may include someone such as an employer, coach, or mentor. It cannot be your parent, guardian, or other relative. This individual must include their contact information and signature on the letter.
## Q. What standardized test results are required? How and when do I submit my scores?

Testing scores are required for the application; please list your most recent ACT or SAT scores. If you are enrolling in a test optional postsecondary program and do not have test scores to report, please indicate that on the application.

**Q. Do I have to be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident in order to apply for a scholarship award?** No. All students who meet the scholarship application criteria are able to apply.
**Q. If I have received a scholarship from NAEHCY in the past, am I still eligible to apply this year?** Students who have received a scholarship from NAEHCY within the past three years are not eligible for a 2026 award.
## Q. What are the eligibility requirements for applying?

To be eligible for the scholarship, applicants must meet the following criteria:

- Applicants must be under the age of 23, as of July 31, 2026.

- Applicants must be actively pursuing undergraduate post-secondary education or trade schools.
- Applicants must be eligible for McKinney-Vento assistance or have experienced homelessness* (while in school) within the last six years. (Applicants must submit a letter verifying their homeless status as part of their application materials.)
Please note, undocumented students who meet the above criteria ARE eligible. However, previous recipients of a NAEHCY scholarship within the past three years are NOT eligible.

The* *definition includes children and youth who are living with friends/relatives temporarily* *(doubled-up) because they lack permanent housing.*

## Q. Can I use the scholarship money at any college and for any major?

*Option 1:* NAEHCY pays an amount designated by you to your school, the remainder of the scholarship is paid via check to you.

*Option 2:* NAEHCY pays you a portion of the scholarship now via a mailed check, and maintains the rest for distribution to you as needed via later checks.

*Option 3:* NAEHCY pays 1/2 of the scholarship to you now, and 1/2 of the scholarship via check at the start of the next academic semester.

## Q. What happens if I receive an award?

NAEHCY will financially support you to attend our annual conference (this year’s location is Nashville, TN) from October 1 - 31, 2026 where your cohort will participate in enrichment and professional development activities, share experiences with NAEHCY stakeholders, and participate in an awards ceremony.

NAEHCY Scholars will be invited to participate in two additional convenings designed to support your educational journey and provide personal and professional enrichment as well as mentorship opportunities.

# 2026 NAEHCY Scholarship FAQs

## Q. How do I apply for a scholarship award?

You must submit all of the following materials by the deadline:

- Completed application (<u>click here to submit online</u>)
- Personal essay
- Unofficial school transcript
- Letter verifying current or former homeless status
- A minimum of one letter of recommendation
## Q. How many scholarships will NAEHCY award this year, and for how much?

The NAEHCY Scholars Program will award at least ten scholarships this year of up to $3,000 each to postsecondary students who have experienced homelessness* and are actively pursuing their post-secondary education. Selected scholars are chosen from a pool of applicants who meet all eligibility criteria and submit all required materials by the deadline.

## Q. When is the deadline for submitting an application this year?

Friday, July 31, 2026 (by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time) is the final submission deadline in order to be considered for a scholarship award.

**Q. When are letters of recommendation and school transcripts due? Can they be sent separately from my application?** We strongly encourage you to <u>submit the application form online</u>, and then email all supporting application materials within one email. This helps the NAEHCY staff with processing your materials. Your email should include these four attachments:
- Personal essay
- Unofficial transcript (If there are barriers to obtaining a transcript, contact us at <u>[contact redacted]</u>)
- Letter verifying current or former homeless status
- Minimum of one letter of recommendation
If you send multiple emails, make sure to include the applicant’s full name and date of birth with each message to ensure our reviewers can accurately identify materials.

## Q. What types of files am I allowed to include as attachments?

Accepted file formats include PDF, Word, JPG and PNG.

**Q. Do my letters of verification and recommendation have to be written by teachers, or can they come from anyone?** One letter verifying your current or former homeless status is required and must be from a local homeless education liaison, school official, outreach worker, shelter provider, religious leader, or other homeless service provider. This individual must include their contact information and signature on the letter. Your letter of recommendation may be written by anyone who knows you well and can attest to your experiences, character, leadership ability, commitment to education while homeless, and/or academic achievement. This may include someone such as an employer, coach, or mentor. It cannot be your parent, guardian, or other relative. This individual must include their contact information and signature on the letter.
## Q. What standardized test results are required? How and when do I submit my scores?

Testing scores are required for the application; please list your most recent ACT or SAT scores. If you are enrolling in a test optional postsecondary program and do not have test scores to report, please indicate that on the application.

**Q. Do I have to be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident in order to apply for a scholarship award?** No. All students who meet the scholarship application criteria are able to apply.
**Q. If I have received a scholarship from NAEHCY in the past, am I still eligible to apply this year?** Students who have received a scholarship from NAEHCY within the past three years are not eligible for a 2026 award.
## Q. What are the eligibility requirements for applying?

To be eligible for the scholarship, applicants must meet the following criteria:

- Applicants must be under the age of 23, as of July 31, 2026.

- Applicants must be actively pursuing undergraduate post-secondary education or trade schools.
- Applicants must be eligible for McKinney-Vento assistance or have experienced homelessness* (while in school) within the last six years. (Applicants must submit a letter verifying their homeless status as part of their application materials.)
Please note, undocumented students who meet the above criteria ARE eligible. However, previous recipients of a NAEHCY scholarship within the past three years are NOT eligible.

**The applicant’s homeless status is defined by the federal McKinney-Vento Homeless* *Education Act, which defines a person considered to be homeless as one who “lacks a* *fixed, regular, and adequate night-time residence.” This includes people living in shelters,* *cars, motels/hotels, campgrounds, or places not meant for human habitation. The* *definition includes children and youth who are living with friends/relatives temporarily* *(doubled-up) because they lack permanent housing.*

## Q. Can I use the scholarship money at any college and for any major?

The scholarship may be used at any degree-granting accredited college or university (or certificate-granting trade program) within the United States. Recipients may study any academic discipline of their choice.

**Q. If I am awarded other scholarships or financial aid, does it affect my eligibility for the NAEHCY Scholarship?** You are eligible for a NAEHCY scholarship even if you receive other scholarships and/or financial aid.
## Q. Will I receive confirmation that my application was received?

Yes, you will receive an auto-generated email confirmation if you submit your application form online.

By early September, you should expect to receive an email confirming whether or not you are being considered for an award. (Incomplete applications will not be considered for an award.) Due to the volume of applications, we cannot guarantee that you will receive this email prior to September 1, 2026.

## Q. When are the winners notified? Are applicants who are not awarded also notified?

Winners will be notified in late August. Those who are not selected will receive notification by early October 2026.

## Q. Where does the funding for the NAEHCY Scholars Program come from?

The scholarships are funded by the NAEHCY Scholar Fund, a 501(c)3 charity and through generous donations from friends and partners.

If selected for an award, you will have three options for the distribution of funds.

*Option 2:* NAEHCY pays you a portion of the scholarship now via a mailed check, and maintains the rest for distribution to you as needed via later checks.

*Option 3:* NAEHCY pays 1/2 of the scholarship to you now, and 1/2 of the scholarship via check at the start of the next academic semester.

NAEHCY Scholars will be invited to participate in two additional convenings designed to support your educational journey and provide personal and professional enrichment as well as mentorship opportunities.

### 2026 Overview

The NAEHCY Scholars Program will award up to ten $3,000 scholarships to postsecondary
students who have experienced homelessness* and are actively pursuing their
post-secondary education. Selected scholars are chosen from a pool of applicants who
meet all eligibility criteria and submit all required materials by the deadline.
